title: Counting dots on a dot plot

beats.say: Four people gave these ratings: two, three, three, and five stars.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Collected numbers like these are called data. Each dot stands for one person.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Data are collected facts or numbers.

beats.say: How do those numbers become a dot plot?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Put each person's dot above their rating on this number line.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The first rating is two. Place its dot above two.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The next rating is three. Place that dot above three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Another person gave three stars. Stack that person's dot above the first.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The last person gave five stars. Their dot goes above five.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: This is a dot plot: one dot for each recorded value.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: Each dot stands above its value. Repeated values stack.

beats.say: Read across for the rating. Count up a stack for how many people.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The three names the rating. The two dots mean two people gave that rating.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Value below. People in the stack.

beats.say: A question can ask us to count several stacks together.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: This dot plot shows the quiz scores of seventeen students.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The dot plot shows the quiz scores of 17 students. Each dot is one of the students. How many had a score at least 6?

beats.say: Each dot is one student. The numbers below are score points.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: How many students had a score at least six?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: My guess is two. I counted only the dots above six.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: That counts students who scored exactly six. At least six also allows larger scores.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: So keep six, and continue to the right through the whole scale.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Gold will mark every dot we count. At six: one, two.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Seven has no dots. Does the count stop there?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: An empty position adds zero. Keep going: eight is also at least six.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: At eight, count one, two more students. Nine has no dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Add the dot counts from six through nine: two, zero, two, zero.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Six and eight are two scores, but they hold four students.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Count every dot in the chosen stacks.

beats.say: Four students scored at least six points.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check the other stacks. Their counts are four, one, two, two, three, and one.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Those are thirteen other students. Thirteen plus four equals all seventeen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Eighteen riders rated a trail. Each dot is one rider.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The dot plot shows the ratings that 18 riders gave a trail. Each dot is one rider. How many had a rating less than 4?

beats.say: How many riders gave a rating less than four? Less than means smaller than.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: My guess is to keep four, like we kept six before.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Test that guess. Is a four-star rating smaller than four?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: No. Four equals four. These three dots must stay out.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Leave four out. Choose the values to its left: zero, one, two, and three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: No rider gave zero. Above one, count one, two, three, four riders.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Above two, count one, two riders.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Above three, count one, two, three, four...
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five, six, seven riders in that stack.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Add those counts: four plus two plus seven equals thirteen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Thirteen riders gave fewer than four stars.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check: three riders gave four stars, and two gave five stars.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Those five riders, with our thirteen, account for all eighteen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Greater than means larger than. It also leaves the named value out.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: At least includes the named value. Less than and greater than leave it out.

beats.say: Champ, sixteen customers rated a lunch. Each dot is one customer.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The dot plot shows the ratings that 16 customers gave a lunch. Each dot is one customer. How many had a rating greater than 3?

beats.say: Greater than means larger than. How many customers gave a rating greater than three?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Larger ratings are to the right of three. I choose four, five, and six.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: What about the dots on three?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: They show exactly three stars. Greater than three leaves both of them out.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Leave the two dots on 3 out.

beats.say: Above four: one, two, three, four, five customers.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Above five: one, two customers. Above six: zero.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Five plus two plus zero equals seven customers.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Seven customers gave a rating greater than three stars.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Can you check against the total?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Outside my count: two at one, five at two, and two at three.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: That's nine outside. Nine plus seven equals all sixteen customers.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: I use the words to choose the values. Then I count every dot above those values.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: A half is one of two equal parts. Half an inch is halfway from zero to one.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Lengths can fall between whole numbers.

beats.say: Length plots can use half-inch labels. Each dot still records one object's length.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The labels name lengths. Count dots to count objects.

beats.say: First, the words tell me which side, and whether the named value counts.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Choose the side. Include the named value only for “at least.”

beats.say: Then I count the dots in those stacks and add the counts.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Count every dot in the chosen stacks. Empty positions add 0.

beats.say: The counted dots and the other dots must account for everyone.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Check that counted dots + other dots = everyone.
